Key audit matter How the key audit matter was addressed in our audit

The Group and Company incurred a loss of KShs 260
million KShs 587 million respectively during the year
ended 30 June 2025, and as of that date, the Group’s
and Company’s current liabilities exceeded their
current assets by KShs 872 million and KShs 628 million
respectively.
The Company was also in breach of the debt coverage
ratio requirement of not less than 0.1 as of 30 June 2025
by having a ratio of -1.21.
The Group and Company’s ability to continue as a
going concern is dependent on (cid:285)nancial support of the
shareholders and the successful outcome of projected
revenues.
We determined going concern to be a key audit matter
because of the signi(cid:285)cant judgements and assumptions
regarding plans put in place by directors to ensure the
Group and the Company continues to have adequate
cash (cid:286)ows to meet their (cid:285)nancial obligations in the normal
course of business.

We evaluated the directors' assessment of the Group’s
and Company’s going concern including plans in place
to manage liquidity requirements for at least 12 months
from the date of approval of the (cid:285)nancial statements. This
included:

subsequent funds received and obtaining evidence of
expected funding.
